questions.question: Which stage often comes before drafting?
A draft is the writer’s what?
When revising an essay, which changes should a writer consider first?
Which task belongs to editing after the ideas and organization are settled?
Proofreading is a final check for what?
A writer lists possible topics before choosing one. What process stage is this?
A writer moves a paragraph so reasons appear in a more logical order. What kind of work is this?
A peer says the essay’s claim is unclear and asks for a more specific one. What feedback addresses?
A student finds a repeated word and replaces one instance with a precise synonym. What revision goal is served?
A writer reads a paragraph aloud and notices a sentence is hard to follow. What is a useful next step?
choices: revise the sentence for clarity and flow

questions.question: Which revision best improves a weak introduction that lists facts but gives no focus?
choices: add a clear context and controlling idea

questions.question: A draft includes evidence but does not explain how it supports the claim. What should revision add?
choices: reasoning that connects evidence and claim

questions.question: A writer’s conclusion introduces a brand-new argument. What revision is most appropriate?
choices: change the essay to a poem
connect the ending to the established claim and implications

questions.question: A writer asks a peer to check whether the steps in an explanation are understandable. What kind of review is this?
A student corrects “recieve” to “receive” after revising the essay’s organization. Which stage is this?
Why should writers consider audience during revision?
choices: choices in detail and tone should fit readers’ needs
every audience requires the same vocabulary

questions.question: A student receives feedback that a paragraph repeats the same reason twice. What revision is strongest?
choices: combine or remove repetition and develop a distinct point
move the paragraph to the title

questions.question: A writer revises a claim after finding stronger evidence that narrows its scope. What does this demonstrate?
choices: evidence should never affect a claim
revision can change ideas as well as wording

questions.question: A writer finishes a draft, checks the assignment purpose, reorganizes two sections, then corrects punctuation. Which sequence is most effective?
choices: revise larger ideas before final editing
edit punctuation instead of checking meaning

questions.question: A peer says “make it better” without identifying a concern. What feedback would be more useful?
choices: rewrite the whole piece without discussion
point to a specific unclear paragraph and explain why
